q: Which donor factor is associated with increased risk of primary graft dysfunction after lung transplant?
why: An ischaemic time over 5.5 hours increases the risk of primary graft dysfunction (PGD).

q: How does primary graft dysfunction typically present?
o: Within 72 hours as an acute lung injury picture
why: PGD appears by 72 hours with an ALI picture; treat supportively, escalating to inhaled nitric oxide or VV-ECMO.

q: How should the pulmonary artery clamp be released at reperfusion of the new lung?
o: Slowly, with increased FiO2 and a fluid bolus
why: Release the PA clamp slowly, increase FiO2 and give a fluid bolus.

q: During single-lung transplant, the pulmonary artery is clamped and the patient becomes hypotensive with a dilated RV. What is the cause?
o: Acute RV failure from the rise in PVR
why: PA clamping raises RV afterload; support with inotropes, inhaled nitric oxide or ECMO.

q: Which indication most often needs a bilateral lung transplant?
why: Suppurative diseases (CF, bronchiectasis) need bilateral transplant so infection cannot spread from a remaining native lung.

q: Which ventilation strategy is used to test the newly implanted lung?
o: Tidal volume 3–4 ml/kg, PEEP 8–10, target SpO2 above 90%
why: Protective one-lung ventilation of the new lung: PEEP 8–10, tidal volume 3–4 ml/kg, SpO2 above 90%, limit FiO2 and fluids.

q: What is the inheritance and basic defect in cystic fibrosis?
why: Autosomal recessive CFTR chloride channel defect causing viscous secretions in the lungs and pancreas.

q: Which organism most commonly colonises the airways of adults with cystic fibrosis?
why: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is typical; Staph aureus, Haemophilus, Stenotrophomonas and Aspergillus are also seen.

q: A teenager has a Nuss (MIRPE) procedure for pectus excavatum. Which requirement differs from a modified Ravitch repair?
why: The thoracoscopic Nuss procedure needs lung isolation and arm abduction; the open Ravitch does not need a DLT.

q: What fluid strategy is used after implantation of the donor lung?
o: Liberal crystalloid to maintain CVP above 15
Fluid restriction to reduce the risk of primary graft dysfunction
why: Restrict fluids after implantation to reduce the risk of PGD.
